parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Assess the significance of the contributions of Iron Age communities to contemporary Zimbabwe.

points.description: Farming: small grains and cattle still matter, though maize and modern methods dominate
Mining and trade: modern mines on ancient workings; minerals still exported
Stone building: World Heritage Sites, tourism, national name and the Zimbabwe Bird
Political structures: chiefs recognised in Chapter 15, strong in rural areas but limited power
Medicine and religion: still important to many, alongside modern medicine and other faiths
Supported overall judgement

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant points or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge and examples, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
The contributions of Iron Age communities remain significant, although some have changed.

In farming, sorghum and millets are still grown and promoted as drought-tolerant crops, and cattle remain central to family life and roora/lobola. However, maize, introduced later, is now the main staple, and modern farming methods are widely used.

In mining, many modern gold mines began on ancient workings, and Zimbabwe still exports minerals, continuing the old pattern of trade.

Stone building is highly significant for identity and tourism. Great Zimbabwe and Khami are World Heritage Sites, the country is named after the houses of stone, and the Zimbabwe Bird is on the flag.

Political structures continue in chiefs, headmen and village heads, recognised in Chapter 15 of the Constitution. They are important in communal areas but have less power than Parliament, councils and courts.

Traditional medicine and religious beliefs remain important to many families, but they exist alongside modern clinics and other faiths.

Overall, the contributions are very significant for identity, culture and rural life, and partly significant in the economy, where modern methods have replaced the old ones.

explanation: Describe (a) and assess (b) Iron Age contributions.
hints: In (b), weigh each contribution and finish with an overall judgement.
